title: Reapply forward force through the same support leg.
brief: The priority is two linked same-leg hops, then a controlled stop. Single-leg hurdle clearance, a motionless single-leg start, a small fore-aft line reversal and a grounded one-leg throw each isolate a contributor. A split-start jump onto a low box rehearses gathering into a supported two-foot finish.

explosive.name: Repeated Single-leg Forward Hops — Two Contacts
explosive.job: Reapply forward impulse from the same receiving leg.
explosive.cue: Hop twice forward on the same foot without an intentional pause, then hold the second landing 2 s; alternate side bouts.
explosive.regress: Shorten each hop; stop for a collapsing intermediate knee/hip or an uncontrolled final contact.
explosive.note: Eight unilateral landings total, four each leg.

explosive.name: Single-leg Forward Hurdle Hop to Stick
explosive.job: Maintain same-leg propulsion and landing around a real clearance constraint.
explosive.cue: Hop from one foot over a very low hurdle to the same foot and hold 2 s, keeping the receiving knee aligned.
explosive.regress: Lower/bring the hurdle closer; stop for clipping, reaching or a free-foot touchdown.

explosive.name: Paused Single-leg Broad Jump to Two-foot Landing
explosive.job: Express a fresh one-leg push without reusing a preceding contact or adding a one-leg finish.
explosive.cue: Hold a shallow one-leg dip still for 2 s, use the arms and jump forward to two feet; hold 2 s.
explosive.regress: Shorten travel and make the start shallower; stop if a re-dip replaces the paused push.

explosive.name: Single-leg Forward–Backward Line Hops
explosive.job: Control a small fore-aft reversal through the same foot.
explosive.cue: Make one forward and one backward crossing of a flat line on the same foot, then settle; repeat on the other foot.
explosive.regress: Narrow the crossing and lower height; stop if the knee locks or balance dominates.
explosive.intent: Small quick crossings, not distance hops

explosive.name: Single-leg Forward Medicine Ball Scoop Toss
explosive.job: Transmit forward force through one planted leg and a controlled pelvis without a landing.
explosive.cue: Stand on one foot with a very light ball low in front; use a shallow hip/knee dip to scoop forward, keeping the free foot clear and torso facing ahead.
explosive.regress: Reduce load/dip; stop for hopping, twisting or loss of foot control.
explosive.intent: Fast release with a light ball; retain the prescribed grounded support
explosive.gate: Comfortable one-leg ball handling; power must not be limited by balance.

explosive.name: Split-Squat Jump onto a Low Box
explosive.job: Gather a lead-leg-biased push into a symmetrical elevated finish.
explosive.cue: From a shallow fixed split stance on the floor, dip once and jump forward/up onto a low box with both feet; hold 2 s, then step down.
explosive.regress: Lower/bring the box closer; stop if the rear leg is trapped, the stance twists or feet land partly off the box.

control.name: Short-Lever Side Plank
control.job: Lightly support frontal-plane trunk/pelvic control during same-leg contacts.
control.cue: Support on forearm and bent knees, lift hips modestly and hold a straight shoulder–hip–knee line while breathing.
control.regress: Shorten the lever/lower effort; stop if the shoulder or back is uncomfortable.
control.intent: Bodyweight/light resistance, easy control; at least 5 clean reps in reserve or comparable ease

control.name: Hip Flexor March Iso Hold — Hand Supported
control.job: Maintain free-thigh position without tipping the pelvis away from the support leg.
control.cue: Use light hand support, raise one thigh to a comfortable march position and hold with ribs stacked over the planted foot.
control.regress: Lower the thigh and reduce effort; stop if lumbar arching or stance-foot rolling appears.
control.intent: Bodyweight/light resistance, easy control; at least 5 clean reps in reserve or comparable ease

strength.name: Hip Thrust — pelvic dumbbell, upper back on bench
Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs

decision: Same-leg links are capped at two per bout; static and elevated two-foot finishes limit additional unilateral receiving demand. The paused unilateral start differs from Class 1's continuous-dip single-leg broad jump; the fore-aft line drill adds an actual reversal rather than more forward distance. Supported single-leg RDL supplies a unilateral hip-strength job without a balance contest. Bilateral squat and walkout remain small; no load or contact progression is earned without actual feedback.
next_job: Class 9 will introduce controlled short-entry bilateral projection; assess actual same-leg response and use an appropriate recovery interval first.
